Topics · Is there a God?

What evidence would be enough for me to believe?

Write your test before reading any answer. Then ask if anything could pass it, and see what is on offer.

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَلَا تَقْفُ مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلْمٌ ۚ إِنَّ ٱلسَّمْعَ وَٱلْبَصَرَ وَٱلْفُؤَادَ كُلُّ أُو۟لَـٰٓئِكَ كَانَ عَنْهُ مَسْـُٔولًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

And do not pursue[745] that of which you have no knowledge. Indeed, the hearing, the sight and the heart - about all those [one] will be questioned.

Translator's notes

[745] i.e., do not assume and do not say.

Quran · Al-Isra 17:36

Translation

I tell you that every idle word that men speak, they will give account of it in the day of judgment. For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.”

Original · Ancient Greek

λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι πᾶν ῥῆμα ἀργὸν ὃ λαλήσουσιν οἱ ἄνθρωποι, ἀποδώσουσιν περὶ αὐτοῦ λόγον ἐν ἡμέρᾳ κρίσεως· ἐκ γὰρ τῶν λόγων σου δικαιωθήσῃ, καὶ ἐκ τῶν λόγων σου καταδικασθήσῃ.

the Gospel (Matthew) · 12:36-37

World English Bible

Do this first, before anyone offers you anything. Decide what would count. If you wait until after you see the evidence, you may move the line without noticing, and so may anyone arguing with you. A fair inquiry fixes its standard in advance. Believing without reasons is not being asked of you here. This verse says the opposite: do not pursue what you have no knowledge of, because hearing, sight and understanding are all answerable. It is a demand for evidence.

A question for you

Write one line: I would believe if...

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَلَوْ فَتَحْنَا عَلَيْهِم بَابًا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ فَظَلُّوا۟ فِيهِ يَعْرُجُونَ١٤ لَقَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّمَا سُكِّرَتْ أَبْصَـٰرُنَا بَلْ نَحْنُ قَوْمٌ مَّسْحُورُونَ١٥﴾

Translation of the meaning

And [even] if We opened to them a gate from the heaven and they continued therein to ascend, They would say, "Our eyes have only been dazzled. Rather, we are a people affected by magic."

Quran · Al-Hijr 15:14-15

Now test your test. Suppose you saw a gate open in the sky. A day later, would you say you had been drugged, or dreaming? These verses say people would: our eyes were dazed, we were bewitched. They describe a mind made up in advance, and any of us can fall into that. A doubt about one strange night can also be honest. So a sign alone may not do what you expect. Whatever would truly convince you has to survive your own doubt the next morning.

A question for you

What would survive your own doubt the next morning?

If you sayAn event everyone sees, repeatedly.
ThenThat is a strong standard. The text asks whether free faith would then remain. That has its Step.
If you sayAn argument I cannot refute.
ThenThen for you reason ranks above the senses. A whole argument begins there.
If you sayMany pieces of evidence pointing one way.
ThenThat is a reasonable standard, and it comes next.
If you sayAlmost nothing.
ThenThat is honest. It is worth asking whether you apply the same standard to what you believe now.

Part 3 of 3

﴿سَنُرِيهِمْ ءَايَـٰتِنَا فِى ٱلْـَٔافَاقِ وَفِىٓ أَنفُسِهِمْ حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَهُمْ أَنَّهُ ٱلْحَقُّ ۗ أَوَلَمْ يَكْفِ بِرَبِّكَ أَنَّهُۥ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ شَهِيدٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth.[1402] But is it not sufficient concerning your Lord that He is, over all things, a Witness?[1403]

Translator's notes

[1402] Or "that He (subḥānahu wa taʿālā) is the Truth." [1403] See footnote of 4:79.

Quran · Fussilat 41:53

Translation

May Yahweh our God be with us as he was with our fathers. Let him not leave us or forsake us, that he may incline our hearts to him, to walk in all his ways, and to keep his commandments, his statutes, and his ordinances, which he commanded our fathers. Let these my words, with which I have made supplication before Yahweh, be near to Yahweh our God day and night, that he may maintain the cause of his servant and the cause of his people Israel, as every day requires; that all the peoples of the earth may know that Yahweh himself is God. There is no one else.

Original · Hebrew

יְהִ֨י יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙ עִמָּ֔נוּ כַּאֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה עִם־אֲבֹתֵ֑ינוּ אַל־יַעַזְבֵ֖נוּ וְאַֽל־יִטְּשֵֽׁנוּ׃ לְהַטּ֥וֹת לְבָבֵ֖נוּ אֵלָ֑יו לָלֶ֣כֶת בְּכָל־דְּרָכָ֗יו וְלִשְׁמֹ֨ר מִצְוֺתָ֤יו וְחֻקָּיו֙ וּמִשְׁפָּטָ֔יו אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוָּ֖ה אֶת־אֲבֹתֵֽינוּ׃ וְיִֽהְי֨וּ דְבָרַ֜י אֵ֗לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֤ר הִתְחַנַּ֨נְתִּי֙ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה קְרֹבִ֛ים אֶל־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵ֖ינוּ יוֹמָ֣ם וָלָ֑יְלָה לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת ׀ מִשְׁפַּ֣ט עַבְדּ֗וֹ וּמִשְׁפַּ֛ט עַמּ֥וֹ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל דְּבַר־י֥וֹם בְּיוֹמֽוֹ׃ לְמַ֗עַן דַּ֚עַת כָּל־עַמֵּ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה ה֣וּא הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים אֵ֖ין עֽוֹד׃

1 Kings · 8:57-60

World English Bible

So here is what is actually offered. No single proof. A set of pointers, which you weigh: that anything exists, that you began, that the world can be understood, that conscience reaches beyond preference, that one book makes claims that can be examined. Each can be answered. The question is whether they add up. This verse promises that signs are in two places, far outside you and within yourself. It sets no deadline. You may find they do not add up. That result is also honest.

A question for you

Where would you like to begin weighing?

If you sayWhy there is anything at all.
ThenThat is the first of the questions.
If you sayHow I would know at all.
ThenA method you can run by yourself.
If you sayThe book itself.
ThenIt has its own test.

The same in the other books

Restraint in the eye is good, good is restraint in the ear, in the nose restraint is good, good is restraint in the tongue. In the body restraint is good, good is restraint in speech, in thought restraint is good, good is restraint in all things. A Bhikshu, restrained in all things, is freed from all pain.

Buddhist texts · Dhp 360-361

Max Müller, 1881

The mountains melt like wax at the presence of Yahweh, at the presence of the Lord of the whole earth. The heavens declare his righteousness. All the peoples have seen his glory.
